_about: Research Desk source catalogue (research_desk.py). Official, free, documented APIs only. 'hosts' is the outbound allow-list: the desk refuses any other host. 'min_interval_s' is the desk's own spacing between requests to that host (at or below the documented limit). 'live_check' records what a real request from this machine returned on the date given; re-run `python research_desk.py check-sources` to refresh it.

pubmed.name: PubMed (NCBI E-utilities: esearch, esummary, efetch)
pubmed.rate_limit: 3 requests/second without an API key, 10/second with one. Every request carries tool= and email= (NCBI asks for both; set the contact email in Settings).
pubmed.used_for: Living Evidence Briefs: search, publication types (incl. 'Retracted Publication'), abstracts.

europepmc.name: Europe PMC REST API
europepmc.rate_limit: No fixed public limit; the desk keeps to 2 requests/second. Responses can be slow (19 s seen) and it answered 503 once during testing, so the desk falls back to its cache.
europepmc.used_for: Living Evidence Briefs: second literature index (adds preprints, flagged as not peer reviewed).

clinicaltrials.name: ClinicalTrials.gov API v2
clinicaltrials.rate_limit: About 50 requests/minute per IP (documented guidance); the desk spaces requests 1.3 s apart.
clinicaltrials.used_for: Trial Finder (condition + region are sent; age and sex are checked on this computer only).

who_don.name: WHO Disease Outbreak News (who.int OData API)
who_don.rate_limit: Not published; the desk keeps to 1 request/second.
who_don.used_for: Triage & Relief: outbreak feed, filtered on this computer by the configured region.

who_iris.name: WHO IRIS (institutional repository, DSpace 7 REST API)
who_iris.rate_limit: Not published; the desk keeps to 1 request/second.
who_iris.used_for: WHO guidance documents listed beside a brief (not counted in the certainty label).

cdc_travel.name: CDC Travelers' Health notices (RSS)
cdc_travel.rate_limit: Static feed; the desk fetches it at most once per cache period.
cdc_travel.used_for: Triage & Relief: travel health notices, filtered on this computer by region.

live_check.result: 200 OK (served as text/html but the body is RSS 2.0)

cdc_open_data.name: CDC open data (data.cdc.gov, Socrata SODA API)
cdc_open_data.rate_limit: Throttled without an app token; not used by default.
cdc_open_data.used_for: Not wired in. The metadata API answered 200 on 2026-11-19, but no single dataset is useful across regions, so the desk uses the travel notices feed instead.

openfda.name: openFDA (drug labels, enforcement reports/recalls, adverse-event counts)
openfda.rate_limit: Without an API key: 240 requests/minute and 1,000/day per IP. openFDA's own disclaimer: do not rely on openFDA to make decisions regarding medical care.
openfda.used_for: Drug reference: label sections quoted verbatim, recalls (watch-list alerts), FAERS reaction counts (not causation).

rxnav.name: RxNorm / RxNav REST API (NLM)
rxnav.rate_limit: 20 requests/second per IP; the desk keeps to 5/second.
rxnav.used_for: Drug name normalisation (RxCUI) and spelling candidates. Candidates are shown, never auto-picked.
rxnav.interaction_api: RETIRED. NLM discontinued the RxNav Drug Interaction API (January 2024). A live request to /REST/interaction/list.json on 2026-11-19 returned HTTP 404. The desk does not compute interactions; it quotes the 'Drug interactions' section of the FDA label instead.

reliefweb.name: ReliefWeb API v2 (UN OCHA humanitarian reports)
reliefweb.rate_limit: 1,000 calls/day per appname. An APPROVED appname is required: request one at https://apidoc.reliefweb.int/parameters#appname and enter it in Settings.
reliefweb.used_for: Triage & Relief: situation reports for the configured country.

live_check.result: v1: 410 Gone ('decommissioned, use v2'); v2 without an approved appname: 403 ('You are not using an approved appname'). Not verified with a real response; the test fixture for a successful v2 answer is synthetic.

triage_systems.name: START - Simple Triage and Rapid Treatment (adults)
triage_systems.origin: Newport Beach Fire Department and Hoag Hospital, California, 1983.
triage_systems.summary: Published field-triage algorithm for adults in a mass-casualty incident. Walking wounded are directed away first; others are assessed for Respirations, Perfusion and Mental status (RPM) and sorted into Immediate (red), Delayed (yellow), Minor (green) or Expectant/Deceased (black). Only airway repositioning and direct pressure on bleeding are done during sorting.
triage_systems.reference: Benson M, Koenig KL, Schultz CH. Disaster triage: START, then SAVE - a new method of dynamic triage for victims of a catastrophic earthquake. Prehosp Disaster Med. 1996;11(2):117-24. PMID 10159733.

triage_systems.name: JumpSTART (children)
triage_systems.origin: Lou E. Romig, MD, 1995 (paediatric adaptation of START).
triage_systems.summary: Paediatric version of START, generally for children who appear to be about 1 to 8 years old. It uses child-specific respiratory-rate limits, a pulse check in place of capillary refill, the AVPU scale for mental status, and a trial of rescue breaths for a child who is not breathing but has a pulse.
triage_systems.reference: Romig LE. Pediatric triage. A system to JumpSTART your triage of young patients at MCIs. JEMS. 2002;27(7):52-8, 60-3. PMID 12141119.

triage_systems.name: SALT - Sort, Assess, Lifesaving interventions, Treatment/Transport
triage_systems.origin: Proposed national all-hazards guideline from a CDC-sponsored expert working group (Lerner EB et al., Disaster Med Public Health Prep. 2008;2 Suppl 1:S25-34, doi:10.1097/DMP.0b013e318182194e). Meets the Model Uniform Core Criteria for mass casualty triage (Disaster Med Public Health Prep. 2011;5(2):125-8, doi:10.1001/dmp.2011.41).
triage_systems.summary: A global sort (walk / wave or purposeful movement / still) sets the order of individual assessment. Lifesaving interventions (bleeding control, airway, chest decompression, auto-injector antidotes) are done during assessment, then each person is assigned Immediate, Delayed, Minimal, Expectant or Dead, with explicit consideration of available resources for the Expectant category.
triage_systems.reference: Lerner EB, et al. Mass casualty triage: an evaluation of the data and development of a proposed national guideline. Disaster Med Public Health Prep. 2008;2 Suppl 1:S25-34. PMID 18769263.

triage_systems.name: WHO ETAT - Emergency Triage Assessment and Treatment (children, health facilities)
triage_systems.origin: World Health Organization; updated guideline 'Paediatric emergency triage, assessment and treatment: care of critically-ill children' (2016).
triage_systems.summary: Facility triage (not mass-casualty) for children arriving at a health facility: Emergency signs, Priority signs, or Queue, with immediate treatment of emergency signs. Included because relief clinics often receive many sick children at once.
triage_systems.reference: World Health Organization. Paediatric emergency triage, assessment and treatment: care of critically-ill children. Updated guideline, 2016.

triage_links_check.result: PubMed, doi.org and who.int links answered 200. The HHS CHEMM pages (chemm.hhs.gov/startadult.htm, startpediatric.htm, salttriage.htm, triage.htm) answered 404, so they are not used.
